Replay

Current framework closure queue

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Final assessment evidenceRecently closed integration gapExplicit support boundaries to retain in the audit

This short queue implements the framework completion plan. The acceptance audit maps the implementation/evidence. This is a finite shared-framework queue, not a game-parity backlog.

The framework-first closure queue is complete. The release assessment maps the final requirements to evidence and retains the decision to keep Replay experimental alongside Kit. The original roadmap's broader game/platform/deployment ambitions are not being marked verified.

The audit may reveal additional concrete shared defects. Each must have a reproducer or an explicit missing API/acceptance criterion before expanding this queue. Do not create tasks just because an old port ledger contains open parity.

Final assessment evidence#

The support envelope records mode/backend/platform coverage, resource bounds, authoring/performance tradeoffs and the P2P control-loss policy. Killing the actual native service clears party readiness after about 10.46 seconds while both existing encrypted links continue to the tick-1200 reference. The freshly built addon passes offline, native network and Chrome execution in a consumer project outside the checkout. See final receipts.

Recently closed integration gap#

Native P2P now accepts an explicit local listener independently of the advertised endpoint. A real forwarded-port TLS/ENet case passes initial play and creator return through a new forwarding port. Setup/recovery onboarding, compatibility policy, native/WASM checked API recipes and tests/replay_framework/run.sh now provide a consolidated entry point. See focused receipts.

The framework audit now has current selected-suite evidence: 362 unit tests, package-specific target/recording checks and one real observer fault/refresh trace. Current observer effects are complete and replay identically on native/WASM; the older trace-less C2 report remains historically unexplained, not an invented fix claim. An optimized arm64 corpus miscompile was isolated to the test factory and has a narrow no-inline workaround with retained evidence.

Native two-player P2P now uses durable enrollment, challenged registration, scoped pair keys and authenticated/encrypted ENet. Real TLS tests cover creator and guest process return, new incarnation, new authenticated generation and retained rollback history. Creator return changes its port and the survivor discovers it. Browser create/join/rejoin still converges after the shared control-router changes. See focused receipts.

Explicit support boundaries to retain in the audit#

  • P2P_Direct is a two-player convenience owner; lower-level runners/RTC mesh and pair/link primitives have different player-count envelopes.
  • Pair-link framing is experimental, lacks forward secrecy against later key compromise and has no independent cryptographic review. Do not advertise a public security certification based on functional tests.
  • Native ENet and browser WebRTC need a common backend for mixed-platform matches. Native RTC extension availability cannot be assumed.
  • Live Steam accounts/GameServer, additional OS/hardware, public TLS/TURN and broader outage profiles need external/platform evidence before being advertised as validated. This does not reopen game-content parity work.
  • Established P2P links can survive background control failure, but new admission needs the service. Automatic failed-control reconnection is explicitly not implemented; the application can close/reopen and restore/rejoin. This is now classified and tested as an experimental support boundary.
